Subject: Records snapshot: retention windows & redaction approaches

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this. We're standing up an internal review of vendor data-handling for a pilot and need concrete answers on two fronts for PII/PHI in Redwood-managed workloads:

1) Retention limits: for a tenant-scoped deletion request, what is the minimum guaranteed window between request and irrevocable removal from all live and cache layers? We need both the "fast-path" (best-effort) and SLA-backed timelines.

2) Redaction options: what options do you support for field-level redaction versus irreversible deletion? Specifically: field masking, pseudonymization (deterministic hashing), tokenization (reversible with KMS), and full physical delete. For each approach we need: approximate impact on model performance for embeddings/generation, a rough cost delta, and whether you can provide audit evidence (deletion certificates / logs).

If you can send a short matrix (high-level) and a sample of the deletion log output we can share with our privacy team, that would speed review.

Can we get a response by EOD Thursday (PST)? Also happy to schedule a 30-min sync if it's easier.

Best,

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Records snapshot: retention windows & redaction approaches

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. TL;DR: we support tenant-scoped irrevocable deletion with audit evidence; multiple redaction tiers are available. Details below and attaching a compact matrix.

Retention / delete timelines
- Fast-path (best-effort): 0–72 hours to purge active stores + KV caches for the tenant, depending on ongoing requests and long-running batches.
- SLA-backed (paid add-on): 7 days guaranteed for complete removal from all serving layers and our short-term caches; archival slices (cold backups) are on a 30–90 day scheduled retention window unless an expedited escrow purge is requested in contract.
- Note: embeddings and derived vectors stored in tenant buckets are treated as primary data for deletion; we do not retain tenant-specific vectors beyond the requested retention window.

Redaction options (high-level)
1) Field-level masking (preferred for reversible anonymization)
   - Mechanism: server-side masking policy applied at ingestion and returned tokens replaced/masked in stored records.
   - Performance impact: minimal.
   - Audit: mutation logs + sample transformed payloads.
2) Pseudonymization (deterministic hashing)
   - Mechanism: salted/deterministic hash per-tenant. Re-identification not possible without salt and mapping; mapping can be held in tenant's KMS if requested.
   - Performance: low impact; embeddings may slightly differ (negligible for most retrieval workloads).
   - Audit: hashing operation logs and salt metadata indicator.
3) Tokenization (reversible with KMS)
   - Mechanism: reversible token store tied to KMS; requires explicit key management.
   - Performance: modest cost increase; reversible so useful for workflows that later require re-linking.
   - Audit: KMS access logs + token access events.
4) Full physical delete (irreversible)
   - Mechanism: deletes tenant data across primary stores, caches, KV, and schedules for cold backup purge.
   - Performance: N/A.
   - Audit: deletion certificate + per-shard deletion logs and snapshot IDs.

Notes on model-serving artifacts
- Model caches (KV/attention caches) are ephemeral per-request; we purge bounded caches on delete. Persistent artifacts (fine-tuned weights or tenant-specific derived models) can be removed or isolated per contract.
- We do not bake tenant PII into base model weights.

Attachments: redaction-matrix-v1.pdf (matrix mapping technique -> evidence type -> SLA), retention-sla-matrix.xlsx (timelines and cost deltas).

Next steps: Marissa / Priyom — can you confirm the contractual SLA language for the 7-day backed delete and what expedited cold-backup purge options we can offer (pricing/lead times)?

Alex — happy to hop on a call Thu or Fri. I can also produce a sample deletion log (sanitized) for your privacy team.

Thanks,

Logan Wright

Thanks Logan — adding the legal and security clarifications. A couple of concrete items CareBridge asked for that we should commit to (or scope as exceptions):

1) Deletion certificate: we can produce a time-stamped deletion certificate for tenant-scoped full deletes that includes shard IDs and confirmation that primary and cache layers were purged. For cold backups, we will provide a scheduled purge date and a follow-up certificate when the purge completes; expedited purge is a professional service with contract addendum.

2) Per-tenant deletion log sample: we'll provide a sanitized example showing the log format we deliver (timestamp, operation, object-id, shard-id, operator-id). See attached audit-evidence-template.docx.

3) SLA language: Priyom, can you pull the exact clause for the 7-day guaranteed delete and the pricing ladder for expedited cold backup purges? We should avoid promising <7 days for all layers unless under a paid expedite.

Alex — we'll get the sample logs and deletion cert template to you within 48 hours. If CareBridge needs a faster turnaround for cold backups purge, we can outline the add-on and lead time in the same package.
